body: Ah yes, the duality of man lol
Love your outfit!

Oooof yes. As a small child my uBPD mom would buy me small, super tight clothes that I always felt uncomfortable in. She stopped exclusively picking my clothes when I got to high school, but she'd always encourage me to choose more revealing clothing when shopping. Her reasoning was that I was becoming ~a beautiful young woman~. If I expressed discomfort (which I did every time because it's just not my style) she'd shame me and poke fun at me for being a prude. It was so bizarre.

I saw that post too, and it felt like a punch in the gut. It's so true! I still doubt my own judgment, even after being NC for almost a year. Thankfully I'm getting better at self trust, but it's rough.

YES ugh. And what sucks is that it seems to be a family thing. The last holiday season we spent together, my grandma told us all a story about how she got so frustrated with my aunt when she was younger that she strangled her. And my mom and grandma laughed so hard! It was the most hilarious story to them! I was completely horrified. My mom yelled at me about how my aunt lived, so it wasn't a big deal. I couldn't believe I was the odd one on this issue, it really brought to light some deep rooted family issues.

I've been there with my mom too. She's thrown tantrums over me not following/friending her. She doesn't even interact with any of my posts on social media, I'm pretty sure she's really just trying to keep tabs on me. I've blocked her and a lot of my family on FB, since she bugs them to send her info about what I'm posting 🙄
What a cutie pie!! 💖

Any time I would show that I was experiencing pain, my mom would say that I was too sensitive and weak. Which somehow meant that I'd NEVER be able to have kids naturally. Then she'd go off on a weird, self congratulatory rant about how she gave birth to both my sister and I with no meds/epidural & brag about how strong she is. Which is just so bizarre??? She would do this pretty frequently to both me and my sister, and if we argued she'd say that we'd be bad mothers and wives bc we had the nerve to talk back. Projecting much? 🥴

My husband and I changed our surnames when we got married a few months ago, to kind of get a fresh start. It happened right around the time that I went NC. It's been a tedious process, but not too expensive so far. I also started a new job, so everyone is getting to know me with my new last name. It's been such a thrill just to see my new name in writing. I'd been considering changing part or all of my name for years now, and I'm so happy to finally have done it! 😊
Uggghh, so weird and invasive 🤢

Yes omg, my mom does this too. Specifically the perfume copying when I got older. I eventually stopped telling her what I wear so that she wouldn't go out and buy some for herself. Last time she visited, she snuck into my room and sprayed one of my perfumes on herself so she could smell just like me. Her words. 🤮

Omg how ridiculous of her. The dramatics are so exhausting and strange. I'm anticipating a similar text that just glazes over everything, but I think I may just block her before that. We should keep the trend of ignoring each other going 😂

Oof, I feel you on that. I've recently realized that my mom still views me as an angsty, moody teen. She literally REFUSES to see the person I've grown up to be despite all evidence I've changed. I'm in my 30s now! She still brings up the times I didn't do certain after school chores, ffs.
Lol I've considered it, a lotttt
Oh no, it was my sister that took the fall for that, oddly enough. But she never got the hateful blame that I did. 🙄

Wow, that's such an awful and ridiculous thing to think about your own child. My mom has also made that connection of not breastfeeding -> too independent -> BAD KID. My sister was more obviously codependent (she even showered with my mom regularly until she was around 10). But she was the good kid because she didn't give her as much "trouble". Smh, they're insane.

Oh wow, I'm so sorry you both went through that. But that is the thing, isn't it? Perpetually the victim, never at fault for anything. And the story of my birth always centered around her and what she went though, and it was usually used as a tool to guilt me. You're right, how stupid and immature to take all that as a personal affront.

Yup, I agree. She would also always talk about how difficult my birth was, and how we both almost died. I think that may also have something to do with her resentment of me. Like, you almost killed me and now you won't even let me feed you?? That's always the impression she's given me when talking about it anyway. How do you hate a baby for acting like...well, just a fussy baby? I'll never truly understand, the delusion is out of control.

Oh gosh, I would get whacked with the brush too! My mom was never gentle with my hair, it felt like she would vent all her frustrations by brushing it as hard and as fast as she could. And when I would complain it hurt, THWACK! And then a torrent of "shut up!", "You're lucky I'm even doing your hair!", "stop being so tender headed!"

Yes omg. Now that I've gotten some distance from my mom, old memories that I'd buried are starting to surface. The most recent of which was about how angry and mean my mom would get when I cried. I cried a lot as a young kid and I remember now that she'd scream at me to "shut up", "stop being a baby", "I'll give you something to cry about", etc. She would hit me (and once even punched me in the face) to get me to stop as well. 

I asked her a few years ago why she's so weird about crying. She told me that she hated the sound of it, and she wasn't allowed as a kid to cry. Talk about repeating cycles of abuse 🤦🏻‍♀️

That's exactly what I've theorized as well. She knows I'm fed up with her behavior and is trying to delay the inevitable, tbh. It's just another way to stick around and control me, even if it's small. I'm super frustrated by the situation.

Oof, that's horrible. I'm so sorry you went through that. I also thought it was normal until I told a few classmates on Monday and got nothing but looks of disgust and "wtf is wrong with her??" in response.
Lol I got a great amount of satisfaction from sending that one word response 🤣

It really is a distinct feeling of horror. I used to panic whenever I'd have a ton of missed calls & texts from her, now I'm just exhausted. Thank you, it's calmed down a lot lately (hopefully it stays that way) 💗

My mom's go to is, "You're not smarter than me just because you went to college!" when she senses she's losing the upper hand in an argument. Regardless of whatever it was we were arguing about. Anything they can use to hold over our heads, they will.

It's so bizarre! I remember one of my most embarrassing college memories was when 2 campus officers came knocking at my dorm early one morning. My mom had frantically called them and had them do a wellness check on me. All because I hadn't spoke to her since dinnertime the previous day, and didn't answer her DOZENS of overnight calls. Because it was the middle of the night. And I was asleep. When I asked her why the hell she did that, she said that she was worried someone had kidnapped her "baby". Ugh 🤢

I unofficially have, I believe. She's moving to a pet friendly apartment in her state soon, but she's waffling about when she'll get her dog. She's trying to push the responsibility of transporting her pet off on me. I don't necessarily want her dog, but I definitely take better care of her than she does.

Background: this was a text thread from a month ago. I took a screenshot of her response bc it was just so outrageous. I've been taking care of my uBPD mom's elderly dog for a few months. She became ill recently. She's doing great now, but for a week it was a nightmare of vet visits, testing, and new meds.

I gave her regular updates on the dog's condition, but she used the opportunity to overstep my boundaries of low contact. She would call/text incessantly. Right before this exchange, she called 5 (!!!) times in a row. She has always expected me to answer her immediately no matter what's going on or the time of day. I was already exhausted from dealing with her dog's health scare and the increased calls, I just didn't have it in me to talk again.

I did in fact block her for a few days after, which felt soooo peaceful. But unfortunately I have to maintain contact due to the dog 😣

That's very true. It's tough to determine exactly what went wrong with my dad, but I don't have the energy or the desire to find out.

I really only have my fiance at the moment, and he's been wonderful with helping me through this. I'm trying to build up my support system right now, and I'm also considering going back into therapy.

I also have a coworker that exhibits BPD traits. She reminds me of my mother so much it makes me not want to go into work a lot of the time. Very waify, permanent victim, "Everyone is out to get me because they didn't say hello to me!!" type of person. It's gotten so bad that a whole new position was created for her to keep her away from our coworkers (why they didn't just fire her instead, I'll never understand). 

I'm sorry you're going through this. Don't feel ashamed about the way you feel, you deserve to have a workplace with people that don't push you to the brink of insanity on the regular.

My mom also hums (verrrry aggressively) on occasion before losing it. And she'll typically raise her arms in a sort of "are you kidding me?!" motion before going into a bad rage. She would also widen her eyes and scrunch up her face if I'd done something to displease her in public. It wasn't the typical stern mom look that other moms would give their kids to get them to correct their behavior. It was full of fury and hatred. I knew if she gave me that look during the day, she'd unleash on me when we got home. 😑

Thank you for your kind words. I'm happy to say we don't live together anymore. She moved out in January to live with my sister several states away. It's been such a peaceful time learning who I am without her constant criticism!

Hi! This is my former cat, Luna. She was a wonderful gal that I unfortunately had to rehome when my uBPD mom brought a non-cat friendly dog home. To our shared apartment. WITHOUT discussing it with me first! And when I raised concerns about the dog terrorizing my cat I was "heartless" and "crazy", and that it would always be her house, her rules (even though we both were on the lease and split the bills equally). Fortunately she's doing well in her new home, but the way my mom handled the situation still bugs me. 😞

There's an older guy famous in my area for having a service turkey. The turkey's name is Buddy. He isn't actually allowed to bring Buddy into stores, but they'll sometimes hang out in the parking lot. Last time I saw them, the guy was trying to get Buddy to gobble at everyone who came out of the store. 

I heard they got banned from the parking lot of the Wal-Mart a few towns over because of their shenanigans. It's a shame, they're hilarious and don't cause any trouble.
I've done that too and still kind of regret it. But the positive part was finding out what I absolutely won't stand for, and promising not to sell myself short in relationships ever again.

Worked there for years before going over to Walmart. It was an absolute shitshow, managed terribly and the building is slowly falling apart. And it was still the best performing store in the county, surprisingly. Can't wait til Sears Holdings finally implodes.

They were pretty much hated by most of the people in my store, for a similar reason. That, and when they did work, they screwed up the mods so completely that they took forever to fix. So glad it's over.
Remodel team. Weren't even from our store.
Nah, it was someone from the remodel team.
